extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of PARI/GP (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and programmers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library/GP functions: definitions, argument rules, return values, examples, and implementation notes across numeric, algebraic, combinatorial and arithmetic routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: liftpol
rubrics_metrics.description: liftpol(x * (1 + O(3)) + Mod(2,3)) — library syntax GEN liftpol(GEN x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how components for which lifts are meaningless (e.g. character strings) are copied verbatim. Example: liftpol(x * (1 + O(3)) + Mod(2,3)) yields (1+O(3))*x + Mod(2,3). Shows behavior with modular components.

rubrics_metrics.name: norm(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic norm of x: the product of x with its conjugate (no square roots are taken), or conjugates for polmods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For vectors and matrices the norm is taken componentwise (not L2-norm). Note: norm of an element of R is its square to be compatible with complex norm. Library syntax: GEN gnorm(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numerator(f, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator of f, defined as f * denominator(f, D). Optional argument D controls over which ring denominator is computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D=1: consider underlying Q-structure and denominator is a positive rational integer. D=variable (e.g. 'y'): treat entries as rational functions in K(y) and denominator is polynomial in y. Examples provided: numerator(x + 1/y + 1/2) returns different results depending on D. Library syntax: GEN numerator(GEN f, GEN D = NULL). Also: numer(GEN x), Q_remove_denom(GEN x, GEN *ptd) (D=1) which also returns denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: oo
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an object meaning +∞ (infinity), usable in functions such as intnum. Can be negated and compared to real numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: +∞ greater than any real number, -oo represents −∞. Library syntax: GEN mkoo().

rubrics_metrics.name: padicprec(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the absolute p-adic precision of object x: the minimum precision of components; returns +oo if x is exact as a p-adic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show mixed O-terms and precision results. Function raises exceptions for objects incompatible with p-adic computations (examples shown). Library syntax: GEN gppadicprec(GEN x, GEN p). Also long padicprec(GEN x, GEN p) returning LONG_MAX if x=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: precision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns floating point precision in decimal digits of PARI object x (if no floating component, returns +oo). If n is present, creates a new object equal to x with floating precision n digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: precision(exp(1e-100)) = 154. Notes: returns floating point accuracy, not series precision; when n smaller than existing precision truncates, otherwise extends with zeros; non-floating types unchanged. Library syntax: GEN precision0(GEN x, long n). Also GEN gprec(GEN x, long n) and long precision(GEN x) where accuracy expressed in words.

rubrics_metrics.name: random({N = 2^31})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a random element in various natural sets depending on type of argument N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior depends on argument type: t_INT -> uniform integer in [0,N-1]; t_REAL -> real in [0,1[ with same accuracy as N; t_INTMOD -> random intmod; t_FFELT -> random finite-field element; t_VEC length 2 [a,b] -> integer between a and b; t_VEC from ellinit over finite field -> random affine point (not uniform on E(k)); t_POL -> random polynomial of degree ≤ deg(N). Uses single internal generator (Brent's XORGEN) with period 2^4096-1, not suitable for cryptography. Seedable via getrand/setrand. Library syntax: GEN genrand(GEN N = NULL). Also GEN ellrandom(GEN E) and GEN ffrandom(GEN a).

rubrics_metrics.name: real(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real part of x. For quadratic numbers this is coefficient of 1 in canonical integral basis (1, ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN greal(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: round(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Rounds x in R to nearest integer (ties to +∞), and sets e to number of error bits (binary exponent of difference between original and rounded value).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to every coefficient at every level of PARI object (unlike other truncation functions). Examples illustrate difference between truncate and round on series. Useful to recover exact integers after approximate computations. Library syntax: GEN round0(GEN x, GEN *e = NULL); also GEN grndtoi(GEN x, long *e) and GEN ground(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: serchop(s, {n = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove all terms of degree strictly less than n in series s. When series contains no terms of degree < n, returns O(x^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: serchop(1/x + x + 2*x^2 + O(x^3)) returns x + 2*x^3 + O(x^3). Library syntax: GEN serchop(GEN s, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: serprec(x, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns absolute precision of x with respect to power series in variable v: minimum precision of components; +oo if x exact as series in v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given. Library syntax: GEN gpserprec(GEN x, long v) where v is variable number. Also long serprec(GEN x, GEN p) returning LONG_MAX if x=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplifies x as much as possible: complex/quadratic number with integer 0 imaginary part converted to real part; polynomial degree 0 converted to constant term. Simplifications occur recursively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful before arithmetic functions which expect integer arguments. GP results are simplified before stored in history (unless automatic simplification disabled). Example: x=2+y-y yields 2; type conversions illustrated. Library syntax: GEN simplify(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sizebyte(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs total number of bytes occupied by the tree representing PARI object x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long gsizebyte(GEN x). Also long gsizeword(GEN x) returning number of words.

rubrics_metrics.name: sizedigit(x) (DEPRECATED)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated function that outputs a quick upper bound for number of decimal digits of components of x (off by at most 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use. For number of decimal digits of positive integer use #digits(x). To estimate size recursively use normlp(x). Library syntax: long sizedigit(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: truncate(x, {&e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Truncates x and sets e to number of error bits. For real x, chops fractional part; for rational function returns integer part (Euclidean quotient) and e not set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies componentwise on vectors/matrices; special uses: when applied to power series transforms to polynomial or rational function by chopping O(X^k); applied to p-adic transforms into integer/rational by chopping O(p^k). Library syntax: GEN trunc0(GEN x, GEN *e = NULL). Also GEN gtrunc(GEN x) and GEN gcvtoi(GEN x, long *e).

rubrics_metrics.name: valuation(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes highest exponent of p dividing x. For integer p, x must be integer, intmod with modulus divisible by p, fraction, q-adic with q=p, polynomial or power series (valuation = min valuation of coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p is polynomial, x must be polynomial/rational function (or power series if x monomial). Valuation of vector/complex/quadratic is min of component valuations. If x=0 result +oo for exact object; for p-adic/power series result is exponent of zero. Other type combos give error. Library syntax: GEN gpvaluation(GEN x, GEN p). Also long gvaluation(GEN x, GEN p) returning LONG_MAX if x=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: varhigher(name, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a variable name whose priority is higher than priority of v (or higher than all existing variables if v omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful because new GP interpreter-created variables have lower priority than existing ones. Examples show incorrect-priority errors and using varhigher to create appropriate variable. Cautions: display name is arbitrary string used only for display and not retrievable; limited number of variables (creating many uses up slots). Advice: reuse existing names and choose sensible priority requirements. Library syntax: GEN varhigher(const char *name, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: variable({x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives main variable of object x (variable with highest priority used in x), and p if x is p-adic. Returns 0 if x has no variable attached. If x omitted returns list of user variables known to interpreter ordered by decreasing priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage and how to test whether variable attached via if (!variable(x), ...). Notes on library mode: use gvar instead of variable for x non-NULL; long gvar(GEN x) returns variable number or NO VARIABLE. Library syntax: GEN gpolvar(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: variables({x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns list of all variables occurring in object x (or all user variables if x omitted), sorted by decreasing priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction if (!variables(x), ...) can test whether variable attached. Examples show duplicate display names arising from varhigher/varlower usage. Library syntax: GEN variables_vec(GEN x = NULL). Also GEN variables_vecsmall(GEN x) returns sorted variable numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: varlower(name, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a variable name whose priority is lower than priority of v (or lower than all existing variables if v omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterpart to varhigher. New interpreter-created variables have lower priority; varlower useful for package authors to avoid failures depending on session history. Cautions: display name arbitrary and not retrievable; limited number of variables; creating many variables consumes slots. Library syntax: GEN varlower(const char *name, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: binomial(x, {k})
rubrics_metrics.description: Binomial coefficient. k must be integer; x can be any PARI object. If x=n non-negative integer and k omitted, returns vector of binomial(n,k) for k=0..n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: binomial(4,2)=6 and binomial(4) returns [1,4,6,4,1]. Library syntax: GEN binomial0(GEN x, GEN k = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: fibonacci(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns x-th Fibonacci number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN fibo(long x).

rubrics_metrics.name: hammingweight(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is t_INT returns binary Hamming weight of |x|; otherwise for t_POL, t_VEC, t_COL, t_VECSMALL or t_MAT returns number of non-zero coefficients of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: hammingweight(15)=4; hammingweight(x^100 + 2*x + 1)=3; hammingweight(matid(100))=100. Library syntax: long hammingweight(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numbpart(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives number of unrestricted partitions of integer n (p(n)). n must be integer and n < 10^15 (with p(n)=0 for n<0, p(0)=1). Algorithm uses Hardy-Ramanujan-Rademacher formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enumerate partitions explicitly use partitions function. Library syntax: GEN numbpart(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: numtoperm(n, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates k-th permutation of numbers 1..n as row vector; k taken modulo n!. Numbering is standard lexicographic ordering starting at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse of permtonum. Library syntax: GEN numtoperm(long n, GEN k).

rubrics_metrics.name: partitions(k, {a = k}, {n = k})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of partitions of integer k as sum of positive integers (parts). Partition represented as t_VECSMALL with parts sorted nondecreasingly. For k<0 returns [], k=0 returns trivial partition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional n,a can restrict partition length and part sizes (n = nmax or [nmin,nmax]; a = amax or [amin,amax]). Default parts positive and zero entries removed unless amin ≤ 0. Examples illustrate bounds on parts and lengths. Library syntax: GEN partitions(long k, GEN a = NULL, GEN n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: permorder(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given permutation x, return its order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: p = [3,1,4,2,5] has order 4. Library syntax: long permorder(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: permsign(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given permutation x, return its signature (+1 or -1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: permsign([3,1,4,2,5]) = -1. Library syntax: long permsign(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: permtonum(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given permutation x on n elements gives number k such that x = numtoperm(n,k); numbering lexicographic starting at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN permtonum(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: stirling(n, k, {flag = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Stirling numbers: first kind s(n,k) (flag=1 default) or second kind S(n,k) (flag=2), for non-negative integer n,k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: s(n,k) = (−1)^(n−k) times number of permutations of n with k cycles; S(n,k) number of ways to partition n elements into k non-empty subsets. Suggestions: if all s(n,k) needed compute product x(x-1)...(x-n+1); if many S(n,k) for same k use generating function (1−x)...(1−kx)^{-1} expansion. Simple helper variants vecstirling, vecstirling2, vecbell provided. Library syntax: GEN stirling(long n, long k, long flag). Also stirling1 and stirling2 wrappers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic functions and factoring engine
rubrics_metrics.description: All arithmetic functions (Euler's totient, Moebius, sigma, etc.) call the factoring machinery after trial division by small primes; factorint includes SQUFOF, Pollard Rho, ECM and MPQS with early exit options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factoring machinery relies on probabilistic primality tests (ispseudoprime); user can set default(factor_proven, 1) to require proven factorizations (may slow PARI). Integer argument N can be given as t_MAT (factorization), or t_VEC [N, fa] to avoid refactoring when multiple arithmetic functions called. Examples: eulerphi accepts factorization objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders in finite groups and Discrete Logarithm functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions to compute order of elements and discrete logarithms in finite groups: ellorder, fforder, znorder for orders; elllog, fflog, znlog for discrete logs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All these functions allow optional argument N representing order of group; N can be t_INT, t_MAT factorization, or preferred t_VEC [N, fa]. For repeated computations it's efficient to initialize and pass group/order data once (example with p large prime, v=[p-1,factor(p-1)] and calling znorder/znlog with v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirichlet characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation and handling of Dirichlet characters on (Z/NZ)* via SNF generators or Conrey generators; characters can be t_INT (Conrey label), t_COL (Conrey logarithm) or t_VEC (SNF generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes decomposition of G = (Z/NZ)*, Conrey generators and Conrey logarithms, and conversion functions: znconreychar (transform t_INT/t_COL to SNF), znconreylog (t_INT/t_VEC -> Conrey log), znconreyexp (t_VEC/t_COL -> Conrey label). Also functions charconj, chardiv, charmul, charker, chareval, charorder, zncharinduce, znconreyconductor exist. Notes: t_COL Conrey logarithms are preferred fastest representation. Conventions for generators for p=2 special cases described.

rubrics_metrics.name: addprimes({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds integers in vector x (or single integer x) to a special table of user-defined primes used for trial division in subsequent factor calls; returns that table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be primes (no internal check even if factor_proven default set). To remove entries use removeprimes. If x empty/omitted returns current list of extra primes. Library syntax: GEN addprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bestappr(x, {B})
rubrics_metrics.description: Using extended Euclidean algorithm variants returns rational approximation a/b to x with denominator limited by B; if B omitted returns best approximation given input accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_REAL or t_FRAC uses continued fractions. For t_INTMOD or t_PADIC performs rational modular reconstruction modulo N returning unique a/b in coprime integers |a|<N/2B and b≤B congruent to x mod N; omitting B chooses B of order N/2. If reconstruction not possible returns []. Applies recursively to components; if any entry fails, returns []. Examples: bestappr(Pi,100)=22/7. Library syntax: GEN bestappr(GEN x, GEN B = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bestapprPade(x, {B})
rubrics_metrics.description: Using extended Euclidean algorithm variants returns rational function approximation a/b to x with denominator degree limited by B; if B omitted returns best approximation affordable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_POLMOD modulo N performs rational modular reconstruction modulo N returning unique rational function a/b with deg(b)≤B congruent to x modulo N. Omitting B sets B = floor(deg(N)/2). For t_RFRAC or t_SER implicitly converts input to t_POLMOD. If reconstruction fails returns []. Applies recursively to components. Examples and internal B choice illustrated. Library syntax: GEN bestapprPade(GEN x, long B).

rubrics_metrics.name: bezout(x, y) (deprecated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for gcdext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcdext0(GEN x, GEN y). Use gcdext instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: bigomega(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of prime divisors of |x| counted with multiplicity (Ω(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: factor(392) shows 2^3 * 7^2 and bigomega(392)=5. For count without multiplicity use omega(x). Library syntax: long bigomega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: charconj(cyc, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite abelian group representation cyc (elementary divisors) and character chi (row vector), return conjugate character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cyc may be any object with .cyc method (e.g., znstar or bnrinit outputs). Characters given as row vectors [a1,...,an] with usual conventions. Examples: charconj([15,5],[1,1]) = [14,4]. For Dirichlet characters on znstar(q,1) Conrey representations are available (see Dirichlet characters section). Library syntax: GEN charconj0(GEN cyc, GEN chi). Also GEN charconj(GEN cyc, GEN chi) when types known (no checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: chardiv(cyc, a, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given group cyc and characters a and b (row vectors), return the character a/b = a * b^{-1} represented appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cyc may be elementary divisors or objects with .cyc. If characters in same format result in same format; otherwise result given as Conrey logarithm. Examples with bnfinit and znstar show conversions and mixed-format results. Library syntax: GEN chardiv0(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN b). Also GEN chardiv(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN b) when types compatible (no checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: chareval(G, chi, x, {z})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given abelian group structure G (supporting discrete logarithm), character chi and element x of G, return value of chi(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed note on representation: characters can be encoded via a fixed ζ∈K* of multiplicative order o and a morphism c:G→(Z/oZ); group decomposed as (Z/o1Z)g1⊕...; vector (ci) defines character via χ(gi)=ζ^{ci(o/oi)}. For Dirichlet characters on znstar(q,1) chi can be t_VEC (SNF), t_COL (Conrey), or t_INT (Conrey label). Behavior depends on optional z: if z omitted returns rational number c(x)/o for x coprime to q normalized 0≤c(x)<o; if x cannot be mapped (not coprime to conductor) returns sentinel −1. (Function description continues in following text.)
